title: T1496.004 — Resource Hijacking - Cloud Service Hijacking
subtitle: This simulation shows a complete cloud service hijacking attack against a small SaaS company.
aria: T1496.004 - Resource Hijacking - Cloud Service Hijacking

nodes.label: Sensitive data
nodes.tip: Sensitive data - What is at risk

steps.title: Phish steals a cloud key
steps.caption: The attacker sends a fake "AWS security alert" to a developer. The linked page copies the login form and harvests a long-lived access key. Mail logs show the new sender domain, nothing more
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: Keys parked for later

steps.title: Quotas raised, service warmed
steps.caption: The attacker requests a sending-quota increase and enables the service. Audit logs record RequestServiceQuotaIncrease. Enablement events like this are rare in normal operations, so the CS-04 rule in Section 5 is the best early signal here

steps.title: SendEmail burst
steps.caption: Hundreds of thousands of phishing emails leave through the company's trusted mail setup. SES and SendGrid dashboards spike, bounce and complaint rates climb, and SPF and DKIM (email authentication checks that prove the message really came from your domain) still pass. A budget alarm set at 80 percent may now fire and reach the SOC
